Organizer validation · RL hackathon kit

The drone does not know the map

It flies attempt after attempt, grows a potential surface out of reward — peaks where it hurt — and the path from A to B gets shorter. This page is the evidence that the kit does what the concept claims, produced by the same run that drew the figures.

  • 125 tests passing
  • 11.5 s full suite
  • 3000 episodes in ~0.2 s
  • 6 invariants guarded
  • Python · NumPy · Matplotlib

02

The surface is built, not revealed

This is the recruiting asset, and the one place the implementation could most easily have cheated. A tree cell is never occupied, so V = max_a Q says nothing about it — the best action never walks into a tree. The lazy fix is to stamp every obstacle at the collision penalty, which draws a beautiful surface that owes nothing to learning.

Instead each tree's height is read back from Q(neighbour, action-into-tree): the pain it actually caused. Trees the agent never hit stay flat, and the peaks rise as it crashes. That is invariant 2 — state is experience, not map — made visible.

03

APF stalls where RL does not

The concept argues that the optimal value function is a navigation function, so reinforcement learning dissolves the local-minimum defect that artificial potential fields have had since Koren & Borenstein described it in 1991. We tested that rather than asserting it: search for seeds where continuous APF provably stalls, then see what each planner does there.

The gains were chosen by sweep, not by convenience. This APF solves 66% of feasible forests and never collides — it fails by stalling, which is the real defect, not a strawman.

Read the fairness column before quoting this

APF and APF+residual both read tree coordinates. They violate invariant 2 on purpose — that track is cartography, kept as a controlled foil, and must never be scored against student submissions. The planner that is handicapped is the map-blind one, and it is the one that wins.

04

Reward, shaping, and why the optimum survives

Reward is −1 per step, −100 collision, +100 goal. The sparse-reward trap is the single biggest risk to the event, so potential-based shaping is part of the core rather than an option: F = γ·Φ(s′) − Φ(s) with Φ(s) = −dist(s, B).

Ng, Harada & Russell's theorem guarantees the optimal policy is unchanged, and the third panel below shows the property it rests on — the shaping term sums to exactly zero around any closed loop, so no cycle can be made profitable. The episodic form also requires Φ(terminal) := 0; without it the guarantee is void, and the collision terminal is where that bites.

Empirically both claims hold. On an empty forest, shaped and unshaped agents converge to exactly the same optimum, L* = 11.3137 — the exact Euclidean diagonal. On seed 0 the shaped agent finds its first good path at episode 2225 against 2400 without.

05

The oracle cannot be beaten

Efficiency η = L*/L is only meaningful if the agent physically cannot out-run the oracle. That is enforced structurally rather than by convention: the environment's collision test and A*'s occupancy test are the same function object, and both apply the identical no-corner-cutting rule. A test asserts neither module defines a radius of its own.

String-pull smoothing exists for drawing only. Scoring against a smoothed path would put η = 1.0 permanently out of reach, so L* stays the grid cost.

06

Sensing and the 3D demo

LIDAR is closed-form ray-vs-circle — no physics engine, no PyBullet. The tabular core never calls it; it exists to render the drone identity the grid world would otherwise lose, and to feed the optional Tier 3 continuous state.

Webots is not installed on the build machine, so the phase-7 bridge was written with no simulator import and unit-tested on its own: policy to waypoint, waypoint to velocity. It follows waypoints rather than raw action vectors, because an 8-way direction command cannot home onto a cell centre — and inside the goal cell the terminal Q row is all zeros, so argmax would happily fly the drone back out.

07

Leaderboard — hidden seeds

Ten hidden seeds, 3000-episode budget, rank lexicographic: learned → safe → optimal → fast. Both trained agents reach full success and zero collisions, so the ranking falls through to optimality and then sample efficiency, which is exactly the intended behaviour.

Sample efficiency is right-censored

Seeds that never cross the bar count as the full budget. An uncensored mean would be inf and erase every difference between agents — the primary RL metric would silently stop measuring anything.

08

Knife-edges worth knowing

These are for the organizers, not the students. Each is currently benign and each would bite if a constant moved.

Suicide is nearly rational

With γ = 0.99, wandering forever is worth −1/(1−γ) = −100 — exactly the collision penalty. The +100 goal breaks the tie and the agent converges, but the margin is zero. If you raise max_steps or lower γ, re-check that the collision rate stays at 0.00.

No generated forest is infeasible

Occupancy is by cell centre with TREE_R = CELL = 0.40, and the sampler's MIN_TREE_SEP = 0.85 makes a sealed wall impossible to generate. So is_feasible is vacuous on generated forests, though it correctly rejects a hand-built palisade. Keep it — it costs nothing and guards future constant changes.

Hidden seeds still ship with the kit

HIDDEN_SEEDS lives in scoring/seeds.py. Before the event, move it to a file that is not distributed to teams. The disjointness test will keep passing either way, so this one will not announce itself.

09

Reproduce

# toolchain
python3.11 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

# every claim on this page, in order
pytest                          # 125 tests, ~11 s
python -m scoring.precompute    # L* + feasibility cache
python -m scoring.harness       # leaderboard on hidden seeds
python -m apf.compare           # APF vs residual vs Q-learning
python -m apf.gain_sweep        # the fairness table for APF gains
python -m viz.report            # all figures + GIFs + facts.json
